title: Intake microgateway for structured logs and tenant affinity
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight intake microgateway service that normalizes incoming structured logs from edge and app-side SDKs, guarantees tenant affinity for per-tenant routing, and emits to both Loki and Elasticsearch-compatible downstreams. The gateway should: 1) negotiate schema versions (via header X-Log-Schema or embedded version field) and apply a small set of canonical transforms (timestamp normalization, trace_id/span_id extraction, severity mapping); 2) enforce idempotency for retries and de-duplication using event fingerprinting and optional idempotency-key header; 3) maintain request->trace linking by ensuring correlation IDs are extracted, validated (traceparent/otlp headers), and propagated into output sinks; 4) provide backpressure and graceful degradation: when downstreams are overloaded route to a persistent Kafka fallback topic and return a 429 with Retry-After where appropriate; 5) support tenant affinity (sticky routing) so tenant-bound logs land in the same shard/pool for ordered reassembly and query locality; 6) emit structured telemetry (ingest p95/p99 latency, decode errors, schema-negotiation failures, tenant-drop rates) to the observability system for SLO tracking.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The gateway accepts application JSON, newline-delimited JSON, and Protobuf-encoded OTLP log records. 2) For 1M qps sustained ingest test with canonical payloads, p95 < 120ms (gateway processing only) and no loss when downstream healthy. 3) Correct extraction and propagation of trace_id and span_id into Loki labels and ES doc fields for 99.99% of test traces. 4) When a downstream signals overload, traffic is reliably diverted to Kafka with no more than 5s extra end-to-end delay for diverted records. 5) Integration tests demonstrating schema negotiation and automatic downgrade path for unknown fields. 6) Config flags to enable/disable idempotency, deduplication, and tenant-affinity at runtime without restart.
implementation_notes:
- Implement as a small Go service using fasthttp for low-latency HTTP ingestion and a worker pool for enrichment. Use a pluggable output adapter interface for Loki (batched push API) and ES (bulk index API).
- Canonical transforms must be schema-driven: add a lightweight schema adapter registry (yaml/json mappings) to canonicalize field names and types.
- Idempotency: compute a stable fingerprint from tenant_id + timestamp window + primary key fields or accept X-Idempotency-Key when provided. Persist short-lived fingerprints in Redis with a ttl to dedupe retries.
- Tenant affinity: maintain a consistent-hash map to route to tenant shards; keep a local cache of shard mappings refreshed from the control plane.
- Backpressure: observe downstream response codes and queue lengths; when threshold crossed, atomically switch to Kafka sink for that tenant and emit a routing-change event to the event bus.
- Observability: instrument with OpenTelemetry metrics and structured DEBUG logs. Expose a /health and /ready endpoint and a /metrics prometheus scrape target.
- Security: accept TLS mutual auth for private deployments; validate JWT claims for tenant ownership where present.
risks:
- Schema drift: tenant sending wildly different event shapes could cause mapping errors; mitigate with default-pass-through and a dead-letter sink.
- Consistency: ordering guarantees across multiple replicas require stickiness and stable hashing; risk of imbalance during re-sharding.
- Cost: running sticky shards increases resource usage for low-volume tenants; mitigate via tenant multiplexing and cold-shard consolidation.
- Latency spikes when switching to Kafka fallback if Kafka producer queues are saturated; require producer tuning and circuit breakers.
- Security: accepting arbitrary structured logs creates risk of PII leakage; need field redaction policy and opt-in PII detection rules.
